- Backend `npm.cmd audit --json`: **0 vulnerabilities** at verification time.

Verification fixed genuine defects: missing `/api/billing/dues` compatibility alias; imaging PUT checking SQL column names instead of submitted values; blank enum filters bypassing validation; PostgreSQL-invalid year-zero dates; acceptance of JWTs without expiry; and enabling an unconfirmed JWT claim contract merely by configuring credentials. The production PostgreSQL pool now uses UTC date boundaries.

## COMPLETE: synthetic security and error checks

- Real signature verification rejects forged, unsigned, wrong-algorithm, wrong-audience, expired and expiry-free tokens under the explicitly synthetic test contract.
- Missing credentials, missing/invalid lab scope and non-authority roles are rejected before queries. Request lab fields cannot override the signed lab scope.
- Production defaults to `authContractVerified: false`. The launcher never opts in, even with a secret and database URL. Missing authentication configuration or an unverified contract returns a controlled `503` without querying the database.
- With the synthetic test authentication enabled, missing database configuration returns `503`; query failures return sanitized errors rather than fabricated records or private database details.
- SQL binds request values as parameters; update identifiers come from a fixed whitelist. Read/update queries include the token lab scope.
- `.env.example` contains local non-secret defaults and empty credential placeholders only. Synthetic credentials and query fixtures live in tests. No live credentials, `.env`, caches, virtual environments or dependency directories are intended for the commit.

## PARTIALLY VERIFIED: calculations and responses

- SQL review and contract checks cover outstanding balances clamped at zero, due-only totals, case-wise rows, mean/median TAT, completed results with known abnormal flags, and non-cancelled test frequency.
- Aging intervals are **0-7, 8-30, 31-59, 60+**. The original 31-60 / 60+ intervals overlap; day 60 belongs only to 60+ to prevent double counting.
- Route tests cover filters, calendar dates, parameterization, laboratory scope, all imaging types, outsource routing, response shapes, empty results, missing records and controlled errors.
- These tests return synthetic database rows. They do **not** execute PostgreSQL arithmetic, establish live Supabase connectivity, verify database constraints, or validate the real Supabase JWT contract.

# 🩺 LabSetu - Backend Integration & API Specification Guide

Welcome to the **LabSetu** backend integration guide! This document is designed for backend developers building or integrating a server (Node.js/Express, Python/FastAPI/Django, Go, Java/Spring Boot, PHP/Laravel, C#/.NET, etc.) with the LabSetu frontend.

---

## 📑 Table of Contents
1. [Architecture & Request Lifecycle](#1-architecture--request-lifecycle)
2. [Frontend Configuration (.env)](#2-frontend-configuration-env)
3. [Authentication & Authorization](#3-authentication--authorization)
4. [Complete REST API Specification](#4-complete-rest-api-specification)
   - [Auth Endpoints](#auth-endpoints)
   - [Appointments Endpoints](#appointments-endpoints)
   - [Diagnostic Reports Endpoints](#diagnostic-reports-endpoints)
   - [Lab Operations & Dashboard Endpoints](#lab-operations--dashboard-endpoints)
   - [Billing & Invoicing Endpoints](#billing--invoicing-endpoints)
   - [Generic Resource Adapter Endpoints](#generic-resource-adapter-endpoints)
5. [Data Models & Database Schemas](#5-data-models--database-schemas)
6. [Included Starter Backend Server](#6-included-starter-backend-server)
7. [API Testing with cURL](#7-api-testing-with-curl)

## 1. Architecture & Request Lifecycle

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│               LabSetu React Frontend                   │
│                                                        │
│  [Views: Citizen / Authority / Auth / Registration]    │
│                           │                            │
│                           ▼                            │
│   [Services: authService, appointmentService, etc.]    │
│                           │                            │
│                           ▼                            │
│       [apiClient: Axios/Fetch + JWT Interceptor]       │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                            │
               HTTP JSON Requests + JWT
                            │
                            ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   Backend REST API                     │
│               (http://localhost:5000/api)              │
│                                                        │
│  - POST /auth/login, /auth/register                    │
│  - GET/POST /appointments                              │
│  - GET /reports, /reports/:id/pdf                      │
│  - GET /lab/dashboard, /billing                        │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            ▼
              ┌───────────────────────────┐
              │  Database (PostgreSQL /   │
              │   MongoDB / MySQL / etc.) │
              └───────────────────────────┘
```

### Transparent Fallback Resilience
The frontend includes a built-in fallback mechanism:
- If `VITE_USE_MOCK=true`, the frontend reads/writes to `localStorage`.
- If `VITE_USE_MOCK=false`, the frontend sends live HTTP requests to your backend server.
- If your backend server goes offline during development, the frontend gracefully falls back to mock storage so screens never crash!

---

## 2. Frontend Configuration (.env)

In `LabSetu/frontend/.env`:

```env
# Point this to your backend server URL
VITE_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:5000/api

# Set to "false" to connect to your real backend server
# Set to "true" to force local mock data
VITE_USE_MOCK=false

# Enable detailed API request/response logs in the browser console
VITE_ENABLE_API_LOGS=true
```

---

## 3. Authentication & Authorization

### Token Standard
- Authentication uses standard **JWT (JSON Web Tokens)**.
- Transmitted in the HTTP header:
  ```http
  Authorization: Bearer <your_jwt_token_here>
  ```
- The frontend `apiClient` automatically extracts the token from `localStorage.getItem('labsetu_token')` and attaches it to all outgoing requests.

### Roles
The system distinguishes two primary roles:
1. `citizen` — Patients accessing test reports, booking home collections, tracking appointments.
2. `authority` — Pathologists, lab directors, technicians, billing receptionists.

---

## 4. Complete REST API Specification

All endpoints are prefixed with `/api`.

### Auth Endpoints

#### 1. Login
- **Method / Path:** `POST /api/auth/login`
- **Description:** Authenticates a citizen or authority user.
- **Request Body:**
  ```json
  {
    "identifier": "admin@labsetu.com",
    "password": "password123",
    "role": "authority"
  }
  ```
  *(Note: `identifier` can be user email, 10-digit mobile number, patient name, or organisation name)*
- **Response (200 OK):**
  ```json
  {
    "success": true,
    "user": {
      "id": "USR-001",
      "email": "admin@labsetu.com",
      "name": "Dr. Shozab Rizvi",
      "role": "authority",
      "phone": "9876543210",
      "labId": "61326885",
      "centerName": "LabSetu Diagnostics"
    },
    "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
  }
  ```
- **Error (401 / 403 / 404):**
  ```json
  {
    "success": false,
    "error": "Incorrect password. Please try again."
  }
  ```

#### 2. Register
- **Method / Path:** `POST /api/auth/register`
- **Description:** Creates a new patient or authority account.
- **Request Body:**
  ```json
  {
    "name": "Rahul Verma",
    "email": "rahul.verma@example.com",
    "phone": "9876543210",
    "password": "SecurePassword123!",
    "role": "citizen",
    "dob": "1995-06-15",
    "gender": "Male",
    "address": "45 Green Park, New Delhi"
  }
  ```
- **Response (201 Created):**
  ```json
  {
    "success": true,
    "user": {
      "id": "USR-1042",
      "email": "rahul.verma@example.com",
      "name": "Rahul Verma",
      "role": "citizen",
      "phone": "9876543210",
      "uhid": "UHID-2026-4821"
    },
    "message": "User registered successfully"
  }
  ```

#### 3. Current User Profile
- **Method / Path:** `GET /api/auth/me`
- **Headers:** `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
- **Response (200 OK):**
  ```json
  {
    "success": true,
    "user": {
      "id": "USR-001",
      "email": "admin@labsetu.com",
      "name": "Dr. Shozab Rizvi",
      "role": "authority",
      "phone": "9876543210",
      "labId": "61326885"
    }
  }
  ```

#### 4. Reset Password
- **Method / Path:** `POST /api/auth/reset-password`
- **Request Body:**
  ```json
  {
    "email": "patient@labsetu.com",
    "newPassword": "NewStrongPassword123!"
  }
  ```
- **Response (200 OK):**
  ```json
  {
    "success": true,
    "message": "Password updated successfully"
  }
  ```

---

### Appointments Endpoints

#### 1. List Appointments

        "type": "Home Collection",

        "amount": 450

  ```

#### 2. Book New Appointment

#### 3. Update / Cancel Appointment
- **Method / Path:** `PUT /api/appointments/:id` (Update status or time)
- **Method / Path:** `DELETE /api/appointments/:id` (Cancel appointment)

### Generic Resource Adapter Endpoints
*(Used by the `useDemoResource(key)` React hook for automatic persistent state sync)*
- `GET /api/resources/:key` — Retrieve saved state object.
- `PUT /api/resources/:key` — Update or overwrite state object.
- `DELETE /api/resources/:key` — Reset state object to defaults.

## 5. Data Models & Database Schemas

### User Entity
```typescript
interface User {
  id: string;               // e.g. "USR-001"
  email: string;            // unique, lowercase
  passwordHash: string;     // bcrypt hashed
  name: string;             // Full name
  role: 'citizen' | 'authority';
  phone?: string;           // 10 digits
  uhid?: string;            // Unique Health ID (for citizen, e.g. UHID-2026-8901)
  labId?: string;           // Laboratory ID (for authority, e.g. 61326885)
  centerName?: string;      // Organization name
  dob?: string;
  gender?: string;
  address?: string;
  createdAt: Date;
}
```

### Appointment Entity
```typescript
interface Appointment {
  id: string;               // e.g. "APT-1001"
  patientName: string;
  uhid: string;
  testName: string;
  labName: string;
  date: string;             // YYYY-MM-DD
  time: string;             // e.g. "09:30 AM"
  type: 'Lab Visit' | 'Home Collection';
  status: 'Confirmed' | 'Completed' | 'Cancelled';
  amount: number;
  bookingDate: Date;
}
```

## 6. Included Starter Backend Server

A fully functioning Express.js reference server is already provided in the `backend/` directory:

```bash
# 1. Navigate to backend directory
cd LabSetu/backend

# 2. Install dependencies
npm install

# 3. Start development server
npm run dev
```

The server runs on `http://localhost:5000/api` with CORS enabled for `http://localhost:5173`.

```bash

  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"identifier":"admin@labsetu.com","password":"password123","role":"authority"}'
```

### 2. Test Citizen Login (Shozab Rizvi)

alter table public.profiles alter column center_id drop not null;

-- 2. Trigger Function: Automatically insert profile with unique UHID using first 4 chars of Auth UID
create or replace function public.handle_new_user()
returns trigger as $$
begin
  insert into public.profiles (id, email, full_name, uhid)
  values (
    new.id, 
    new.email, 
    coalesce(new.raw_user_meta_data->>'full_name', 'Patient'), 
    'UHID-' || substring(new.id::text from 1 for 4) || '-' || to_char(current_date, 'YYYY')
  )
  on conflict (id) do update set
    full_name = coalesce(excluded.full_name, profiles.full_name),
    email = excluded.email,
    uhid = case 
      when profiles.uhid is null or profiles.uhid = 'Pending' or trim(profiles.uhid) = '' 
      then excluded.uhid 
      else profiles.uhid 
    end;
  return new;
end;
$$ language plpgsql security definer;

-- 3. Trigger: Automatically invoke handle_new_user on every new user registration
drop trigger if exists on_auth_user_created on auth.users;
create trigger on_auth_user_created
  after insert on auth.users
  for each row execute procedure public.handle_new_user();

-- 4. Retroactive fix for existing accounts with null, empty, or 'Pending' UHID
update public.profiles
set uhid = 'UHID-' || substring(id::text from 1 for 4) || '-' || to_char(coalesce(created_at, current_date), 'YYYY')
where uhid is null or uhid = 'Pending' or trim(uhid) = '';

-- Also synchronize public.patients table for existing accounts
update public.patients
set patient_code = 'UHID-' || substring(id::text from 1 for 4) || '-' || to_char(coalesce(created_at, current_date), 'YYYY')
where patient_code is null or patient_code = 'Pending' or trim(patient_code) = '';
